subject: Deployment options & initial cost sketches for FinTechCorp
messages:

Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: deployment needs & next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Alex and Jane,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clarity on your use case (real-time fraud explainability + nightly batch embeddings for analytics). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Key constraints you mentioned
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for the real-time scoring path
- Data residency: customer PII must remain in your VPC for production
- Predictable monthly cost is important for procurement (preferred fixed commit)

2) Deployment options we discussed and initial suitability
- Hosted API: fastest to launch, pay-as-you-go (per-token). Good for piloting but likely won’t meet your PII residency needs in prod.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools (monthly commit) — can meet latency and economics for steady throughput; isolates compute from other customers.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control over network and keys — best for strict compliance but higher ops overhead and longer procurement.

3) Immediate ask from us
- Can you share a 7-day sample of request volumes (calls/min) broken out by inference type (real-time scoring vs batch embedding)? If you can’t share raw logs, an anonymized histogram will do.
- Who on your procurement side should we loop in for committed capacity pricing?

4) Next steps
- I’ll circulate a lightweight cost model (attached) showing per-token vs capacity economics across three traffic scenarios (pilot, steady-state, peak burst).
- If helpful, book a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Monica to validate latency SLOs and networking for Private/VPC options.

We’ll aim to have a trimmed cost view by Monday so you can share with procurement.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Alex/Laura/Jane —

Attached is an updated cost sketch (20260214_fintech_cost_model.xlsx) with the blended-hosted row you requested plus a sensitivity table for sequence length and KV cache hit rates. High-level findings: 

- For pilot volume (approx 250k tokens/day), Hosted per-token costs are lowest short-term — ~ $X/day — and require no commit.
- For steady-state (expected 20M tokens/day) Dedicated reserved capacity at a 1-month commit gives ~35–45% unit-cost savings versus Hosted per-token, assuming a 3:1 burst cushion. Exact $s depend on average sequence length and batching.
- Private/VPC pricing leverages an enterprise platform fee + infra commit; unit-costs are similar to Dedicated once provisioned, but procurement & setup add ~6–10 weeks and one-time onboarding costs.

Questions for your team before the technical deep-dive: 
- Confirm whether the PII must be processed inside your network for all inference types or only for prod real-time paths.
- Any hard requirements on audit/log retention (e.g., 7 years)? That will affect cost of observability add-ons.

Proposed meeting slots next week for technical deep-dive with Monica and our infra lead:
- Tue 02/17 09:00–10:00 PT
- Wed 02/18 13:00–14:00 PT
- Thu 02/19 11:00–12:00 PT

Please pick a slot and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Aditya

Hi Alex/Laura —

Quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

- For p95 < 250ms on real-time scoring we need to validate model size and KV cache warm-up characteristics. If your model is >13B with average seq len 512, Dedicated with optimized kernels is the likely minimum to hit that SLO consistently.
- Networking: Private/VPC option will require a peering/VPN configuration and a short audit of your egress rules; I’ll prepare a checklist.
- Cost modeling tip: the most sensitive variables are (1) model sequence length distribution, (2) cache hit rate, and (3) steady-state concurrency. If you can provide anonymized histograms for those we’ll produce a tighter committed-capacity recommendation.

I’ve attached a short one-pager comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private from an operational perspective.

I can take the Wed 02/18 13:00 PT slot — Monica (infra) and I will join. Marissa: can you own the procurement intro and pricing sheet for the dedicated reserve scenarios?

—Monica
